chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Ja'far ibn Abdullah al-Muhammadi, from Abu Rawh Faraj ibn Qurrat, from Ja'far ibn Abdullah, from Mas'adat ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) gave a sermon in Medina, praised Allah, extolled Him, and sent greetings upon the Prophet and his family. Then he said: 'As for what follows, indeed Allah, Blessed and High, did not break the backs of the tyrants of time except after a period of respite and ease, nor did He mend the broken bones of the nations except after a long period and affliction.'

O people! In what you have faced of calamities and endured of mishaps is a lesson, and not every person with a heart is intelligent, nor every person with an ear is a listener, nor every person with a seeing eye is a seer.

Servants of Allah! Do good in what your eyes see, then look at the plains of those whom Allah drove by His knowledge, who were upon the Sunnah of the family of Pharaoh, people of gardens, fountains, plantations, and spacious places. Then look at what Allah ended for them after prosperity and joy, command and prohibition. And for the one among you who is patient, the end is in the Gardens. By Allah, they will be immortalized, and to Allah belongs the end of all affairs.

Oh wonder! And why should I not be astonished at the mistakes of these sects despite their differing arguments in their religion? They do not follow the trace of a Prophet, nor imitate the action of a Successor, nor believe in the unseen, nor excuse faults. Goodness among them is what they know, and evil is what they reject. And each one of them is an imam to himself, holding onto what he sees with firm bonds and decisive reasons. So they do not cease in injustice, and they will not increase except in error, not attaining nearness, and they will not increase except in distance from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. They are companions to one another and confirm one another.

All that is alienation from what the Unlettered Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) bequeathed, and aversion from what was conveyed to them from the news of the Originator of the heavens and the earth. They are people of regrets, caves of doubts, people of desires, misguidance, and doubt. Whom Allah leaves to his own self and opinion, he is trustworthy with those who are ignorant of him, not accused by those who do not know him.

How similar are these to livestock whose shepherd is absent from them! Oh regrettable are the deeds of my Shiites after the nearness of their affection today. How some will humiliate others after me, and how some will kill others, scattered tomorrow from the root, falling upon the branch, hoping for victory from a direction not its own. Each party from among them takes hold of a branch. Whichever way the branch leans, they lean with it.

Indeed Allah, and to Him belongs the praise, will gather these for the evil of the day of the Banu Umayya, just as He gathers the clods of autumn. Allah will bring them together, then settle upon them a peak, and the flow of its torrent will not be stopped by a pile of boulders. Allah will shake them in the depths of valleys, then make them flow as fountains in the earth. He will take from one people the rights of another, and enable a people in the dwellings of another, to displace the Banu Umayya and lest they usurp what they usurped. Allah will undermine a pillar through them and break through them the folded tents of Iram, and fill the valleys of olives with them.

By the One who split the grain and created the soul, that will surely happen. It is as if I hear the whinnying of their horses and the humming of their men. By Allah, what is in their hands will melt after their elevation and dominance in the land, just as fat melts over fire. Whoever dies among them dies misguided, and to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will be referred whoever among them proceeds. And perhaps Allah will gather my Shiites after the scattering for the evil of the day of these. And not for anyone upon Allah, Mighty is His Remembrance, is the choice, but to Allah belongs the choice and the command all together.

O people! Indeed, those who claim Imamate from those not deserving of it are many. And had you not neglected the bitterness of the truth, and had not weakened from belittling the falsehood, those not like you would not have become daring against you, nor would he have become strong against you who became strong in digesting obedience and removing it from its rightful people. But you will be lost, just as the Children of Israel were lost in the time of Musa ibn Imran (peace be upon him).

By my life, your being lost will be multiplied after me, tenfold what the Children of Israel were lost. And by my life, had you completed after me the duration of the Sultanate of Banu Umayya, you would have gathered to the Sultan calling to misguidance, revived the falsehood, left the truth behind your backs, cut off the nearest from the people of Badr, and connected to the farthest from the sons of war for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

And by my life, when what is in their hands melts, the purification for the reward will be near, the promise will be close, and the period will end. And the two-tailed star will appear to you from the East, and the luminous moon will shine for you. So when that is, return to repentance, and know that if you follow the rising of the East, he will lead you on the paths of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family).

So you will be cured from blindness, deafness, and dumbness, and you will be sufficient from the burden of seeking and arbitrariness, and you will cast off the heavy weight from the necks. And Allah will not distance except the one who refuses, is unjust, and takes what is not for him. And those who do wrong will know by what a reverse they will be overturned.
ai.seo_question: What does the sermon of Amir al-Mu'minin say about the mistakes of the sects and the future of the Shiites?
ai.summary: This sermon by Imam Ali (as) in Medina serves as a diagnostic critique of religious deviation, contrasting the stability of divine guidance with the self-referential error of sects that lack a fixed reference point. It specifically laments the fragmentation of the Shiites and their political passivity, which allowed the Umayyads to consolidate power, while prophesying their eventual vindication through the 'Star of the East' (often interpreted as the Mahdi or a key figure of deliverance). The text underscores the Shia theological principle that true success lies in adhering to the Ahl al-Bayt rather than relying on individual reasoning or political opportunism.
